sentences.text: Aktiogavialis possessed an elongated, squat quadrupedal body featuring a long, laterally flattened tail and a specialized narrow snout.
The holotype specimen UPRMP 3094 — the specific fossil the species is based on — dates to around 28 million years ago.
These remains were unearthed in the San Sebastián Formation along the Río Guatemala in Puerto Rico.
The genus was described by Vélez-Juarbe and colleagues in 2007, with the type species A. puertoricensis introduced that same year.
Marine sediments and nannofossils within the deposit indicate a marine distribution for A. puertoricensis.
Aktiogavialis belongs to the family Gavialidae.
Two species are known: the type species A. puertoricensis and A. caribesi, which was described in 2018.
The animal lived from the Oligocene to the Miocene in the region now known as the Caribbean, specifically from the Rupelian to the Tortonian stages between 33.9 and 7.246 million years ago.
